title: CDP-accelerated a11y for Chrome targets (roadmap)
desc: Replace slow Windows UIA bridge with CDP Accessibility API for Chrome targets. Same tree screen readers see, 5-10x faster. Interface unchanged -- same a11y commands, routing decision inside Core.
steps: WHY: Windows UIA path = COM cross-process marshaling (slow). CDP path = local WebSocket to Chrome internals (fast). Both read the same Chrome internal AX tree. Screen reader users, CDP, and UIA all see the same accessibility tree -- but CDP is the most direct and accurate route.

ARCHITECTURE: a11y command receives grap -> detect CDP port -> if Chrome+CDP: route to Accessibility.getFullAXTree (find/read) + Input.dispatch* (click/type) + Runtime.evaluate (set-value/invoke). If no CDP: fallback to current UIA path. Non-browser apps always UIA.

MISMATCH CASES TO HANDLE: (1) aria-hidden=true -- hidden in AX tree (both UIA and CDP AX), visible in CDP DOM. (2) Shadow DOM -- UIA bridge flattens/misses, CDP Accessibility handles correctly. (3) Cross-frame iframes -- UIA misses cross-origin, CDP targets by frameId. (4) Timing: UIA COM lag can return stale state after React render; CDP query is current-state.
ROADMAP [P0]: Chrome target detection via CDP port in grap -> route find/read through Accessibility.getFullAXTree instead of UIA. Perf target: under 100ms for find on any page.

ROADMAP [P1]: a11y click/invoke via CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent + Input.dispatchKeyEvent. a11y type via Input.dispatchKeyEvent per char. a11y set-value via Runtime.evaluate with React-compatible value setter.

ROADMAP [P2]: a11y scroll via Input.dispatchMouseEvent scroll. a11y screenshot via Page.captureScreenshot (higher quality). a11y wait via CDP Page events (load/DOMContentLoaded) instead of polling UIA.

ROADMAP [P3]: expose backendDOMNodeId in a11y find output for Chrome targets -- enables direct DOM-to-AX correlation. a11y find --cdp-node option shows: UIA-path + DOM tag#id.class + ARIA role/name side by side.
